PullRequest.Title: Don't reattach restored terminal editors to another window's terminal
PullRequest.Body:

Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341502

- Pass the pid saved with a restored terminal editor through `attachToRevivedProcess`.
- When there is no revived process, reattach by the editor's original persistent process ID only if that process still has the saved pid. IDs restart from 1 whenever the pty host restarts, so the ID can belong to another window's running terminal; a mismatch now creates a new terminal, the same as a missing ID.
- Keep attaching revived processes by their new ID without a pid check, since reviving starts a new process.
- Keep the current behavior when the saved pid is unknown (`0`), and for terminals moved between windows or picked with Attach to Session, which still attach by ID only.
- Clear the shell pid when a relaunch installs its new process. A terminal editor saved before the new shell is ready now stores pid `0` instead of pairing the new ID with the previous shell's pid, which the check above would refuse.
- Add an optional `pid` to `IPtyService.attachToProcess`, checked on the pty host, and forward it through `PtyHostService`.
- Register `PtyService`'s RPC trace listeners so the service can be constructed in leak-checked tests.
- Export `LocalTerminalBackend` so its reattach routing can be tested.
- Remote terminal editors restore through `attachToProcess` directly and are not changed here; the `attachToRevivedProcess` docs now say only the local backend checks the pid.

## How to test

1. Launch VS Code with only folder B open, run **Terminal: Create New Terminal in Editor Area** three times, close B's window, then quit VS Code.
2. Launch VS Code with folder A, create three terminals, and run `sleep 600` in the third.
3. Use **File > New Window** and open folder B.

Expected: B starts new terminals, A's terminals stay in A, and `sleep` keeps running. The Pty Host log shows `Persistent process reconnection "N" failed Pty N has pid X, expected Y`. Before this change, B showed A's running terminals as editor tabs, and typing in or closing them affected A.

Also check that reloading keeps the same shells, that **Terminal: Relaunch Active Terminal** in an editor terminal followed by a reload reattaches to the relaunched shell, and that quitting and reopening restores the terminal history.

Validation:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/terminal/test/node/ptyService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalProcessManager.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/electron-browser/localTerminalBackend.test.ts`: 17 passing. The new tests fail without the changes: without clearing the pid, a relaunched terminal reports `{ id: 2, pid: 1001 }` before it's ready, and with the previous backend routing a mismatched pid attaches to the other process.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/terminal/**/*.test.js"`: 763 passing, 14 pending. `--runGlob "**/terminalContrib/**/*.test.js"`: 2749 passing, 176 pending. `--runGlob "**/contrib/tasks/**/*.test.js"`: 90 passing, 5 pending.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed.
- In Code OSS built from this branch with real shells:
  - The steps above refused all three saved IDs (`Pty 2 has pid 5226, expected 99559`), started new terminals in B, and left A's terminals and `sleep` running.
  - Reloading kept the same editor and panel shells, relaunching an editor terminal and then reloading reattached the relaunched shell, and quitting and reopening revived the terminals with their history.
  - With the pty host paused in the relaunched process's `start` (`--inspect-ptyhost`), the periodic save stored the editor as `{"id":4,"pid":0}`. After killing the renderer and choosing **Reopen**, the editor reattached the relaunched shell. On the previous commit, the same steps stored the previous shell's pid, refused the relaunched shell, and started a second one.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The saved `pid`, and `0` when it was unknown, come from [`TerminalInputSerializer._toJson`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorSerializer.ts#L37-L52).
- Comparing against the live pid holds across reloads because an already started persistent process reports its pid again when a window reattaches, in [`PersistentTerminalProcess.start`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L880-L884).
- Skipping the check for revived processes follows [`PtyService._reviveTerminalProcess`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L284-L309), which starts a new process and maps the old ID to it per workspace for [`getRevivedPtyNewId`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L561-L569).
- Limiting the check to `findRevivedId` follows [`TerminalEditorService.reviveInput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorService.ts#L238-L244), the only place that sets it.
- Clearing the pid where the new process is installed follows from [`persistentProcessId`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L132), which reports the new ID as soon as [`createProcess`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L364) installs the process, while `shellProcessId` only changes in its [ready handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L381).
- A terminal editor can be saved during that gap because storage also flushes when idle, every minute, in [`AbstractStorageService.doFlushWhenIdle`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/storage/common/storage.ts#L376-L385).
- The expected-failure `ErrorNoTelemetry` message style comes from [`PtyService._throwIfNoPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L669-L675).
- The location and leak-checked style of `localTerminalBackend.test.ts` follow [`localPty.test.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/electron-browser/localPty.test.ts#L19-L123).
- Reading and setting private test state with `Reflect` follows [`terminalProcess.test.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9ebdca5c15f666ab336ca0b0421f5ee25bf1cbe0/src/vs/platform/terminal/test/node/terminalProcess.test.ts#L51-L55).

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore local terminal editors when serialized terminal state was revived in the current pty host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor deserialization creates a terminal instance; process creation waits for the local direct proxy, then getRevivedPtyNewId and attachToProcess must complete before LocalPty.start can replay/start the terminal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Look up the revived persistent-process ID in the pty host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per restored local terminal editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same getRevivedPtyNewId RPC was issued once per restored editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before selecting the process to attach.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attach to the revived persistent terminal process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per restored local terminal editor with a revived mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same attach RPC followed the revived-ID lookup; the diff only omits PID validation for the newly revived process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the terminal can start/replay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One restore path per serialized terminal editor; effective cardinality is two pty-host RPCs per editor. The PID argument does not add an operation when a revived ID exists.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple editor inputs may restore concurrently, but _connectToDirectProxy coalesces them on one DeferredPromise. The two RPCs for each terminal remain sequential; the diff adds no aggregate concurrency or limiter bypass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The direct proxy connection is coalesced and reused. Revived-ID lookup is a pty-host Map read keyed by workspace and old ID; successful and missing lookups are not separately cached in the renderer, but each restore invokes the path once and there is no retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch and direct-proxy call sequence are explicit, and successful revived restores retain the same RPC count and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of restored editor terminals varies by workspace, but it does not alter the before/after cost per terminal.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: successful revived restores retain two sequential RPCs per editor, shared connection establishment, and the same process start/replay behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a local terminal editor after a pty-host restart when no revived-ID mapping exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer performs the revived-ID lookup and then an attach RPC. If the original ID still maps to the saved PID, restore continues normally. If it maps to another PID, the attach is refused and the existing fallback resolves the launch configuration/environment and creates a replacement terminal process before the editor becomes usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the pty host for a revived ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per restored local terminal editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lookup occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before deciding whether to attach by revived or original ID.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attach to the original persistent-process ID while sending the saved PID for validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per editor without a revived mapping; the extra PID is a scalar in the existing request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same attach RPC was issued without PID validation and could attach a different window's process after ID reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A matching attach completes restore; a mismatch fails immediately before PersistentTerminalProcess.attach.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and start a replacement shell through _launchLocalProcess after attachment is refused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one replacement process per restored editor whose saved ID now belongs to a different PID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A colliding ID incorrectly attached the already-running process, so no replacement shell was created; missing IDs and other attach failures already used this same fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The replacement must be created and started before that terminal is usable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup and attach attempt per restored editor. Replacement shell creation scales with the number of actual stale-ID/PID collisions, bounded by the number of restored editor terminals, with no retry or repeated attach.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editor restoration can initiate independent terminal restores concurrently; connection establishment is coalesced, while any required replacement processes may be created concurrently as they were for any pre-existing attach failure. The diff changes which stale-collision attaches enter that fallback, not its scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold restore coalesces direct-proxy startup; warm restore reuses it. The pty-host process Map provides the authoritative ID/PID state. There is no negative-cache need because each restored input attempts attachment once and then clears attachPersistentProcess before replacement creation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: PID mismatch is checked in the pty host before attach, and TerminalProcessManager explicitly falls back to one process creation when attach returns undefined.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Stale-ID collisions require a pty-host restart plus ID reuse and are uncommon; a workspace may restore several affected editors at once. Exact shell startup cost is platform/profile dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added replacement process is the required bounded behavior for a stale collision, occurs once per affected editor without retry, and matching-ID restores add only a constant-time PID comparison to the existing IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Relaunch a terminal and serialize its editor while the replacement shell is starting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Relaunch creates the replacement process, installs it, resets shellProcessId locally, registers process listeners, and invokes start. The terminal becomes ready when onProcessReady supplies the new PID. Editor serialization is off the process-start critical path and reads current IDs synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the newly created or attached terminal process via LocalPty/remote pty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start RPC per terminal creation or relaunch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same start RPC occurred; the manager could temporarily expose the prior shell PID alongside the new persistent ID.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the editor's persistent ID and current shell PID into workspace editor state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small object per persisted terminal editor when workbench storage serializes editor state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Serialization already occurred and could pair the new persistent ID with the previous shell PID during relaunch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on shell startup; storage serialization reads the reset value and emits PID 0 until ready.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scalar assignment per process creation/relaunch; serialization remains one small JSON object per persisted terminal editor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work or boundary concurrency is introduced. Existing process creation/start remains one operation for the relaunched terminal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The PID is intentionally unknown until the authoritative ready event and then stored for subsequent serialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the assignment is synchronous and the existing ready handler restores the PID before queued input is flushed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The duration of the shell-ready gap varies, but the diff adds no work proportional to that duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: clearing one scalar prevents stale serialization and neither adds boundary calls nor increases serialized size.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose PtyService after pty-host shutdown or leak-checked construction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PtyService disposal shuts down persistent terminals and disposes registered emitters/listeners. Registering the seven trace-listener subscriptions only changes cleanup ownership.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed number of trace event subscriptions per PtyService instance, independent of terminal count and event volume.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; listener lifetime is now explicitly tied to service lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _traceEvent is called for a fixed set of service events and the added _register only records their disposables.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the change is fixed-size lifecycle bookkeeping.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; this is a cleanup-lifecycle improvement with constant retained state and no added per-event work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and complete diff pages. Traced local revived restore, stale-ID fallback, remote compatibility, relaunch serialization, direct-proxy coalescing, pty-host IPC, shell creation, and trace-listener disposal. The diff adds a constant PID comparison to an existing attach RPC and intentionally creates at most one replacement shell for each proven stale collision; no high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression-fix signal was found.
